subtype: Approach: adjusting when the schedule feels like a burden [Revision]
passage: "Papa, I am changing my chart," Kavitha announced, flute case in hand. Hemant looked up. "Why?" "Seven days makes it homework. Yesterday I played badly on purpose so it would finish sooner." "That does not sound like fun." "It is not! So four days: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday. The other days I play only what I feel like." "Will you keep to four?" "Yes, and I will tick them." She stuck the new chart over the old one. On Wednesday, with no rule at all, she picked up the flute anyway and played a film tune for ten happy minutes.

qa.q: Which four days did Kavitha choose?
qa.a: Kavitha chose Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday.

qa.q: What was Kavitha feeling about seven-day practice, and what showed it?
qa.a: Resentful and bored, since she played badly on purpose so that it would finish sooner.

qa.q: What could Kavitha do if four days starts to feel like a chore too?
qa.a: Shorten the sessions or vary what she plays, because enjoyment is what keeps her going.

qa.q: How might Hemant see Kavitha's change?
qa.a: With patience and understanding, since he asked questions and let her decide, and he can see she still wants to play.

grounding: A girl finds daily practice makes the hobby a chore, so she cuts it to four days and leaves the others for free play.

subtype: Approach: adjusting when the schedule feels like a burden [Revision]
passage: I'm Deepika, and in January I promised my violin teacher I'd practise every single day. By March I was dreading five o'clock. I'd sit with the violin on my lap, watching the clock, and play scales as if they were a punishment. One evening Avni, who calls me Didi and follows me everywhere, asked why I looked so sad playing the thing I used to love. That stung. So I made a new chart: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday for proper practice, half an hour each. On the other days the violin is for whatever I want, film songs, silly tunes, or nothing at all. Last Friday I played Avni a cartoon song just for fun. I'd forgotten it could be fun.

qa.q: Which days are for proper practice now?
qa.a: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday, half an hour each.

qa.q: How did Deepika feel about five o'clock by March?
qa.a: Deepika dreaded it, feeling bored and weighed down, as if practice were a punishment.

qa.q: What else could Deepika try if four days still feels heavy?
qa.a: Shorten a session or mix a fun song into the practice days, adjusting again instead of quitting the violin.

qa.q: How might Avni see the change?
qa.a: Avni probably enjoys getting a cartoon song just for fun and is glad to see her Didi happy while playing again.

grounding: A girl describes daily violin practice becoming a chore and changing to four days a week with free play on the others.

subtype: Approach: adjusting when the schedule feels like a burden [Revision]
passage:
Notes on Arohi, Saturday junior batch
For two months Arohi has done the home practice sheet every day, as I asked. This month I noticed her feet were correct but her face was flat, and twice she asked if class could end early. On Thursday she stayed back and said, "I love dancing, but practice every day feels like homework." We made a change together: home practice on Monday, Wednesday, Friday and Sunday, and on the other days she can dance however she likes, to any music, or rest. Today, for the first time in weeks, she was smiling through the adavus, and she asked to show me a few steps she had made up to a film song. I will check in again at the end of the month.
— Nirmala, dance teacher

qa.q: Which days are home practice now?
What did Arohi's flat face and wish to end class early suggest?
qa.a: They suggested she felt bored and weighed down, with the joy of dancing squeezed out by practice every day.

qa.q: Why might four practice days work better for Arohi than seven?
qa.a: Free days bring back choice and play, so dancing feels like hers again, while four days is still enough to keep improving.

qa.q: How does Nirmala seem to see the change?
qa.a: Nirmala seems glad to see Arohi smiling again, but plans to check in at the end of the month rather than assume it is fixed.

grounding: A dance teacher's note shows a girl whose daily practice felt like a chore changing to four days with free days between.
